chapter: Hollywood, Ken Murray and the Penguin years
title: The best band: Galbraith and the overseas group (second version)
summary: The overseas band was among his best, and Frank Galbraith modeled his playing on Armstrong.

story.theme_name: Remembering the early trumpeters and their styles
story.community_name: Trumpeters I admired: rating the horn players

blocks.x: Of all the little bands that you had over the years, which do you think was the best, musically?
Including the one I went overseas with, you mean?
Any of them.
That was the greatest band I was ever with.
You mean musically?
Musically I would say there was two or three of them that was comparable
to each other, but the one that I took overseas, Frank Galbraith, Willard Brown, Budd Johnson, Huey Long, John Brown on bass, Ed Cornelius, Kenny Bryant on piano.
That was the best?
One of the--it was larger.
When you listen to these records that I made at the Queens Terrace and also at the Sunnyside Horseshoe--
That would have been a very good band, although Galbraith is a better trumpet player than Bob Carroll.
Oh yes; oh yes.
He was a hell of a good trumpet player.
He was every bit as great as Louie Armstrong ever was.
What was the matter with him?
He loved Louie Armstrong's songs so much that he tried to play like
Louie instead of getting his own style. He was one of the greatest things I ever heard in my life.
How was he as a person?
Wonderful. He was one of the nicest guys I ever dealt with.
How did you come to get him? He only worked with you on that overseas tour?
He worked with me for a year on the overseas trip.
But he didn't work for you in the civilian band?
He came back and recorded with me.
